key_insight: Reduced-order models paired with quantum transport can preserve nonlinear flow dynamics while making per-step rotation counts scale polylogarithmically with grid resolution at fixed model dimension and polynomial degree.
engineering_relevance: The approach makes reduced-model polynomial degree a practical trade-off between flow-model accuracy and early fault-tolerant quantum resource costs.
method: Fit polynomial reduced-order flow models using sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics.
Encode probability-density evolution with Walsh-synthesized Koopman–von Neumann transport.
Estimate end-to-end runtime and physical-qubit requirements using surface-code resource models.
evidence_signal: For a saturating cylinder wake, the study estimates 1.62 hours on about 560,000 physical qubits for 1% relative RMS field error against the radial model, and demonstrates nonlinear radial transport on IBM hardware with reference-circuit noise mitigation.
watch_item: These are fault-tolerant resource estimates rather than demonstrated end-to-end runtimes; three-coordinate wake estimates range from hours to weeks, and the stated 1% error is measured against a reduced radial model.
paper_title: Nonlinearity-preserving quantum simulation of flows in the early fault-tolerant regime
